title: Payment Arrangements Calculation Note — First Installment Collected by a New Payment Method
content:
When a plan under Payment Arrangements moves to a newly authorized payment method, the number of the first installment that method collects is worked out as follows.

## Definition

The hand-over starts from the installments the plan's payments already cover: the hand-over covered amount is the installment payments received under the plan less the installment payments returned, less the down payment, plus the type's partial-payment tolerance, so that an installment short by no more than the type's tolerance counts as covered, and the hand-over next installment is one more than the number of whole regular installments that amount covers, the covered amount being divided by the regular installment amount and any fraction dropped.

When the hand-over next installment is the installment of the plan's most recent returned installment payment, the new method collects it only if it is the plan's schedule anchor installment and the days from the handling date to the schedule anchor date are more than the set-up notice plus the set-up notice extension plus the set-up notice return allowance; otherwise the new method first collects the installment after it. When the hand-over next installment is any other installment, the new method first collects that installment.

The set-up notice is 5 days, the set-up notice extension is 2 days and the set-up notice return allowance is 2 days. The days to the schedule anchor date are counted in business days, Monday to Friday, after the handling date: each Monday-to-Friday day after the handling date, up to and including the schedule anchor date, counts as one.

## Inputs

| Input | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| Installment payments received, installment payments returned | Amounts on the plan's installment history |
| Down payment, regular installment amount | The plan record |
| Partial-payment tolerance | The arrangement type's product figure |
| Installment of the most recent returned installment payment | The latest returned installment payment on the installment history |
| Schedule anchor installment and schedule anchor date | The plan record |

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

A monthly plan has a down payment of 200.00 and a regular installment of 150.00 on a type whose tolerance reads 5.00. Payments received total 650.00 and one payment of 150.00 was returned; the most recent returned installment payment was for installment 3.

- Covered amount: 650.00 less 150.00 less 200.00 plus 5.00 is 305.00.
- 305.00 divided by 150.00 is 2.03; dropping the fraction leaves 2 whole installments, so the hand-over next installment is 3 — the installment of the most recent return.
- The notice to be exceeded: 5 plus 2 plus 2 is 9 days.
- The plan's schedule anchor installment is 3. With the handling date on a Monday and the anchor date on the Monday two weeks later, the count is 10 business days; 10 is more than 9, so the new method first collects installment 3.
- With the anchor date on the Monday one week later instead, the count is 5 business days, not more than 9: the new method first collects installment 4.
- Had the hand-over next installment been any installment other than the one of the most recent returned installment payment, the new method would first collect that installment.
